title: Speech of President Arroyo on the Ceremonial Signing of the Omnibus Power Bill, June 8, 2001
text:
Speech of Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo President of the Philippines On the Ceremonial Signing of the Omnibus Power Bill

[ Delivered at the Ceremonial Hall, Malacañang, June 8, 2001 ]

THE OMNIBUS POWER BILL: RATE REDUCTION THROUGH GREAT COMPETITION

Una’y gusto kong pasalamatan ang mga senador at kongresista na tumawid ng party line at nagtulung-tulong para maipasa ang Power Reform Bill. The passage of this bill demonstrates that healing is more productive than hatred. So, “To God be the glory”.

Dahil sa batas na ito, matitigil na natin ang napakalaking ibinibigay ng gobyerno sa NAPOCOR bawa’t taon bilang subsidy. Malaki pong halaga iyan. This law unburdens government from having to maintain and operate generating plants. At Php38 billion annually, government subsidies to the power sector could be used to fund other services. This amount can build more than a hundred fifteen thousand classrooms. This, almost a hundred twenty seven thousand hectares, can put up 76,000 low-cost houses or construct 6,300 kilometers of road. This aspect to me is most significant, for it enables government to stretch its finances to meet other basic needs that our people should have immediately.

Dahil sa batas na ito, sana hindi na magkakaroon ng problema ang gobyerno na maghanap ng dagdag na puhunan para sa energy sector. At the core of this law is the framework for greater competition and the provision of a level playing field for power generator.

Dahil sa batas na ito, ay malulutas ang utang ng NAPOCOR. Kung hindi pumasa ang Power Reform Bill, patuloy sana ang paglobo ng utang na ito. Iyan na po ang ilan sa mga dahilan kung bakit masyadong mataas ang presyo ng ating kuryente at isa sa pinakamataas sa buong Asya. Ito ang dahilan kung bakit napakamahal ng presyo ng mga bilihin. Sa pagpasa ng power reform bill, magkakaroon ng kumpetisyon. Inaasahan natin, bababa ang presyo ng kuryente.

Our reputation as having one the most expensive electricity rates in Asia will hopefully change, with the law’s mandates of rate reduction of around 30 centavos per kilowatt-hour for residential consumers. The law also provides for a reduction in industrial power rates.

Kung bababa ang presyo ng kuryente, dapat susunod ang pagbaba ng presyo ng mga bilihin o kaya man lang maiwasan ang malubhang pagtaas pa ng mga presyo. Magiging competitive tayo sa ibang bansa. Marami po ang pabor sa batas na ito at marami din ang tutol. Pinakinggan ko pong mabuti ang dalawang panig. Pinakinggan din sila ng mga kongresista at senador. At sa isang makasaysayang boto, nagpasiya ang ating mga matatalinong mambabatas na ipasa ang Power Reform Bill.

Many of our countrymen and even some legislators who voted for this new law believed, that this new law can still stand some improvement. In particular, they want the law to level the playing field more in the power industry, and to institute additional safeguards to protect consumers.

I believe these are valid concerns. And I am directing the incoming Secretary of Energy, Vicente Perez, who is right here, to conduct public hearings to determine if further amendments are needed, and what amendments are needed to further protect the public interest. And with the indulgence of our senators and congressmen who have worked so hard, if the hearings come about with conscientious amendments, then I hope they will indulge me, when I certify in the 12th Congress as urgent, the enactment of this needed conscientious, amendment to the law.

May magkasama pong ginhawa at sakit ang batas na ito. May ginhawa po at ang mga ginhawa na nandiyan ay magsisimula kaagad, iyong pagbaba ng ating electric bills. Ang mga sakit naman ay inaasahan nating unti-unting mawawala. Ngunit kung hindi po natin inalis o ginamot ang karamdaman lalo pang gagrabe ang mga sakit. Gagamitin po natin ang perang mase-save gaya ng sinabi ko kanina, para sa mga prayoridad natin. Katulad ng murang pabahay, libreng gamot, imprastraktura, and mass education. Pasisiglahin natin ang ekonomiya at ang kalidad ng ating buhay.

Maraming salamat muli sa mga senador at mga kongresista. Ladies and gentlemen of the 11th Congress, aside from thanking you for passing this bill, I also offer you the deep appreciation of the Filipino people for all your accomplishments during this Congress.

This Congress has set many “firsts”. This is the first but hopefully, the only Congress of our country that has worked with two administrations.

And, it is this Congress that will finally see the passage into law of what is perhaps, the longest running bill in our history, because it spanned three administrations and two Congresses, indeed, the longest running bill in Philippine contemporary legislation, the Electric Power Industry Reform Bill, which will soon become Republic Act 9136.

I am glad, that the soon to be Republic Act 9136 is the product of the joint efforts of this immediate, past and the present administration. It was in the past administration that this bill reached the Bicameral Conference Committee level. This administration has ensured that the work done to push the bill would not come to naught. As the child of two administrations, this law should prove that when the interest of the Filipino people is at stake, Congress and the Executive Branch will readily set aside politics and join hands to benefit our people.

Let it also be said here that this administration will continue to implement sound policies started by previous administrations.

Maraming salamat din sa mga NGO na sumuporta sa atin. Ang pagpasa ng Power Reform Bill na pinagdebatehan noong nakaraang siyam na taon ay isang demonstrasyon ng bagong diwa ng pagtutulungan ng mga Pilipino. Ipagpatuloy po natin ang diwang ito ng pagkakaisa para sa ating bayan, para sa ating kabataan, para sa ating kinabukasan.

Today, we also witness the signing into law of Republic Act 9137, or the Supplemental Appropriations for Fiscal Year 2001. Nagagalak akong pirmahan ang panukalang batas na ito, na bukod sa ibang bagay ay magbibigay ng limang porsiyentong dagdag sa sahod ng mga government workers. This supplemental budget is vital to the operations of the bureaucracy of a total Php10.9 billion in the supplemental budget, Php1.45 billion will cover the second installation of the salary increases for the Philippine National Police, as mandated by Republic Act 8551; five hundred million pesos covers the increase in the monthly old-aged pensions of veterans and surviving spouses under Republic Act No. 7696; and, one billion pesos will go to the deficiencies in the appropriation of foreign-assisted projects, as well as a counterpart requirement of projects that will be implemented starting this year.

The bulk of the supplemental budget amounting to 7.95 billion pesos will cover salary deficiencies and adjustments. Of these amounts, 4.15 billion pesos will be used to pay 5,000 teachers hired in fiscal year 2000, the increase in government share of health and insurance premiums of government employees, retirement benefits for PNP personnel, and the deficiency in the regular retirement benefits of our government personnel. The remaining amount of Php3.8 billion, will be used to cover the five percent across the board increase of all national government employees.

Ako na ang unang nagsasabi na hindi pa rin sapat ang umento para lubusang tapatan ang pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin. Ako na rin ang unang aamin, na matagal nang dapat ibinigay ang nasabing umento sa mga government workers, dahil matagal ng nalampasan ng private sector salary scale ang salary scale ng public sector.

Isang napakaimportanteng bahagi ang government service sa ating programa para sa reporma. Hindi natin matatapos ang ating mga piano kung wala tayong matatag, masisipag, at edukadong government workers. Taun-taon ay nababawasan tayo ng magagaling na government workers, dahil sila ay lumilipat sa private sector, o di kaya naman ay umaalis patungong ibang bansa. Bilang isang ekonomista, hindi ko sinisisi ang kanilang desisyon dahil prayoridad nila ang interes ng kanilang pamilya. Makatuwiran ang kanilang desisyon. Pero sa katagalan, ang kawalan ng edukasyon at disiplina ng government workers ay makakaapekto sa paghahapit ng serbisyong bayan sa mga mamamayan. Ganoon pa man kailangan nating pataasin pa ang kalidad ng government service sa pamamagitan ng training, improved recruitment at better pay. Sinisikap natin ang sapat na sahod ng mga government workers sapagkat malaki ang kanilang serbisyo sa bayan. Kung sabagay, ay hindi laging salapi ang kabayaran ng public service. Ang makatulong sa pagbuo ng bansa ay isang uri ng tinatawag nating psychic income, isang kasiyahang loob na mahigit pa sa salapi. Pero nariyan pa rin ang pangangailangan sa perang nasa bulsa o nasa bangko.

Bukod sa Php3.8 billion na salary increase na binanggit ko para sa mga government workers, uulitin ko, dadagdagan din ng batas na ito ang sahod ng mga pulis, mga guro, ang pension para sa mga beterano, at popondohan din ang retirement benefits para sa mga kawani ng pamahalaan.

Kaya gusto kong pasalamatan muli ang Kongreso sa kanilang pagpasa ng supplemental budget na nagkakahalaga ng Php10.9 billion. Pinasasalamatan ko ang mga magigiting na senador at congressmen na nag-oovertime para siguraduhing magkaroon ng dagdag na umento ang mga masisipag na empleyado ng pamahalaan. Salamat po sa inyong lahat, mga senador at congressmen.

You, the members of the 11th Congress have made your work as legislators and statesmen, with more than 400 new laws to your credits. These last two laws to be signed soon, are testaments to the sincerity and the political will of both the Legislative and Executive Branches in searching for enduring processes, systems and plans that has positive impact on our people’s lives.

I am particularly happy that after I became President, Congress passed a hundred three bills including the last two bills, and 20 of them are of national application.

Since I have been President for only a hundred forty days, this means that during the time you worked together, congressmen and senators, you passed almost one law per day. And I hope that the 12th Congress wherein many of you will still sit, will be as productive.

Take a bow, ladies and gentlemen of the 11th Congress and a cheery applause of the Filipino nation. It has been my great honor to have worked with you. At sa lahat ng ating mga kapuwa Pilipino, bayan magkaisa.

Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat.

Source: University of the Philippines Diliman Library
